follow-an-event.title: Filter and transform each event
follow-an-event.note: Read the predicate and mapper contracts: one decides which records continue; the other chooses the value emitted.

follow-an-event.title: Build and execute a bounded dataflow
follow-an-event.note: Follow the source, output and execution interfaces used by the editor and the course collect helper.

evolve-an-event-schema.title: A mapper applies your schema policy
evolve-an-event-schema.note: The callback implements normalization and rejection; Bytewax does not infer the amount units or schema version.

evolve-an-event-schema.title: Finite test input
evolve-an-event-schema.note: Inspect how the fixed record sequence becomes the input to the graph.

read-a-partitioned-log.title: The Bytewax Kafka source
read-a-partitioned-log.note: Read how topics and partitions become input. The lab uses this connector against librdkafka’s simulator, not an Apache Kafka deployment.

read-a-partitioned-log.title: Send records and inspect offsets
read-a-partitioned-log.note: Inspect explicit partition selection and the delivery callback.

stream-live-through-kafka.title: Consume and update live keyed state
stream-live-through-kafka.note: Follow how the child engine reads records, maintains keyed totals and reports observations.

stream-live-through-kafka.title: Produce a later event
stream-live-through-kafka.note: Read queueing, callback and flush behavior before treating a producer call as downstream completion.

retain-or-compact-a-log.title: Compaction is a log policy
retain-or-compact-a-log.note: Compare the broker’s documented compaction contract with the authored retained_log function. The Python helper does not run a broker compactor.

give-consumers-their-own-position.title: Assign and commit a position
give-consumers-their-own-position.note: Read the distinction between fetching a record and recording the next offset for a group.

route-and-quarantine.title: Separate good and invalid records
route-and-quarantine.note: The decoding callback labels the result; branch splits records according to a predicate.

expand-and-rekey.title: Change cardinality, then choose a key
expand-and-rekey.note: Read how flat_map emits several items per input and how key_on defines the accumulator’s ownership.

choose-the-right-clock.title: Engine clock contract for comparison
choose-the-right-clock.note: clock_windows is an authored assignment model. These engine clocks show how event timestamps and system time are selected in an actual window operator.

close-a-window.title: Window membership and closing
close-a-window.note: Read window length, offset and the clock’s progress contract. The helper uses SlidingWindower even when slide equals width.

merge-a-session.title: Sessions use a gap rule
merge-a-session.note: Read when events extend or merge a session and how the clock affects closure.

wait-for-late-events.title: Watermark progress and late output
wait-for-late-events.note: Read the clock waiting duration and the window operator’s down and late outputs.

correct-a-late-result.title: Framework late-data rules for comparison
correct-a-late-result.note: The corrections helper is an authored revision policy. Compare it with a framework’s window retention and late-data rules without treating them as the same API.

keep-state-by-key.title: Key ownership and callback state
keep-state-by-key.note: Read the keyed stream contract and the callback’s (updated_state, emitted_value) result.

build-a-materialized-view.title: Store the latest accepted revision
build-a-materialized-view.note: The callback implements revision checks and tombstones; these are authored policies over native keyed state.

enrich-a-stream.title: Look up a field in the mapper
enrich-a-stream.note: The mapper performs a Python dictionary lookup. This is a current local lookup, not a versioned temporal join.

join-changing-streams.title: Join insertion and emission modes
join-changing-streams.note: Read insert_mode and emit_mode separately. This fixture chooses final emission over bounded input.

count-the-join-output.title: Interval join contract for comparison
count-the-join-output.note: interval_join is an explicit nested-loop course implementation. Use the framework guide to compare time bounds and retention requirements.

look-up-the-past.title: Temporal joins and version history
look-up-the-past.note: temporal_lookup is an authored valid-time lookup. Compare its version selection with the documented temporal-table contract.

detect-event-sequences.title: Build an application state machine
detect-event-sequences.note: The callback tracks sequence history; this exercise does not invoke a built-in CEP engine.

replay-without-double-counting.title: Deduplicate, then accumulate
replay-without-double-counting.note: Inspect identity selection, retained seen-state and final accumulation as separate operations.

forget-state-deliberately.title: Key ownership and callback state
forget-state-deliberately.note: Read the keyed stream contract and the callback’s (updated_state, emitted_value) result.

forget-state-deliberately.title: State retention policy
forget-state-deliberately.note: The helper uses logical timestamps and returns None to discard state. It does not configure a background TTL service.

recover-after-a-failure.title: Configure real Bytewax recovery
recover-after-a-failure.note: Read recovery partition setup and the source snapshot contract. The helper waits for a checkpoint, kills the engine and restarts it within this one experiment.

retry-with-a-budget.title: A mapper can implement retry policy
retry-with-a-budget.note: The retries are authored, bounded attempts with calculated delays. They are not built-in durable retries or measured sleeping time.

measure-operation-effort.title: Python container operations
measure-operation-effort.note: The helper instruments explicit algorithms. A language reference describes operations; it does not promise universal constant-time performance for every key or implementation.

measure-latency-and-batching.title: Choose the measured boundary
links: Google SRE: latency, traffic, errors and saturation
measure-latency-and-batching.note: latency_run is a deterministic schedule model. Read the monitoring guidance before interpreting average completion, first-item delay or tail latency as interchangeable metrics.

when-the-consumer-falls-behind.title: Demand and bounded queues
when-the-consumer-falls-behind.note: queue_run is an authored admission/service model. It does not execute the Reactive Streams request protocol or measure a network queue.

budget-for-recovery.title: Recovery capacity and state size
budget-for-recovery.note: recovery_capacity computes a fluid capacity model. Compare its spare-rate assumption with actual restore, replay and state-loading costs.

run-a-bounded-backfill.title: Read explicit partition offsets
run-a-bounded-backfill.note: Read the source range and distinguish consumed records from idempotent visible sink rows.

run-a-bounded-backfill.title: Transform the bounded input
run-a-bounded-backfill.note: The helper replays a bounded range and applies an authored sink keyed by record ID.

resolve-the-streaming-incident.title: Key ownership and callback state
resolve-the-streaming-incident.note: Read the keyed stream contract and the callback’s (updated_state, emitted_value) result.

resolve-the-streaming-incident.title: Separate operator state from application rules
resolve-the-streaming-incident.note: Identity checks, validation, late-event classification and output revisions are implemented in the callback.
